body:
Five Opus 4.8 agents each read the full SG + `_WORLD_BRIEF` + a tightened sweep brief, then used judgment (not pattern matching) to soften voice where the language was more confident than the truth supports.

## Edits (5 total)

- **L489** — 'put Liquid's models inside billion-dollar production stacks' → 'are putting' (Mercedes targets H2 2026, not deployed)
- **L530** — thesis sentence scope corrected: 'Every competitor in 4.3–4.5 is a transformer' → 'Almost every ... (IBM Granite 4.0, a hybrid, is the partial exception)'. Granite was already named in Ring 4 of the SG, so the original absolute was internally contradicted.
- **L834** — Ring 3 distribution: 'consumer-device shipping proof is one OEM (Mercedes)' → 'consumer-device proof is one OEM design win (Mercedes, with production targeted for H2 2026)'. Mercedes isn't shipping yet.
- **L901** — Battlecard B: 'Liquid's sovereign-deployment depth ... exceeds IBM's' → 'can match or exceed IBM's'. Flat untagged superiority claim.
- **L1226 (glossary)** — Insilico entry '1,000 pharma benchmarks' → '200+ pharma tasks'. Harmonizes with the body card at L741 updated in fact_check_5.

## Method note
The first calibration wave (PR #9) used per-chunk audit files and produced 15 edits. This sweep used a different workflow — agents got the full 1505-line file as context, no audit, no grep, just judgment against `_WORLD_BRIEF`. The lower edit count (5 vs 15) reflects that PR #9 already absorbed the high-confidence calibrations. The remaining edits are the ones that needed full-doc context to spot (the Granite/thesis-scope tension and the glossary/body 1,000-vs-200 number mismatch in particular).

## Verification
- HTML parses cleanly (0 errors)
- Line count unchanged (1505)
- All 38 `<span class="t">` wrappers preserved
- No locked facts touched

## Reports
Per-chunk reports at `/home/user/workspace/factcheck/calibration_5/SWEEP_C{1..5}.md`.

body:
## What
Calibration pass on the SG. Not a fact-check (Wave 4 did that). This wave tightens *how confidently* claims are stated, per user directive: **"always better to understate slightly than overstate."**

## Trigger
User caught the anchor sentence overstating: "frontier-quality intelligence... proven in production by" was wrong on two counts:
1. Liquid markets **"frontier-grade performance"**, not "frontier-quality intelligence" ([Nanos launch blog](https://www.liquid.ai/blog/introducing-liquid-nanos-frontier-grade-performance-on-everyday-devices))
2. "Proven in production" was a stretch for 3 of 4 partners — only Shopify is in real production today; Mercedes targets H2 2026; Brilliant Halo began shipping 2026; AMD is platform/investor partner

## Method (Wave-4 chunk pattern)
1. Refreshed `_WORLD_BRIEF.md` §2 with the calibrated anchor as global context
2. Authored `_CALIBRATION_BRIEF.md` (directive + patterns + locked-facts list)
3. Spawned 5 parallel Opus 4.8 calibration agents (C1–C5), one per audit chunk, each isolated to its own line range. Each agent read both global docs FULL + its per-chunk audit FULL before editing.
4. Parent reviewed combined diff, committed, pushed.

## Edits (15 total)
**Anchor (L446 / 452 / 456):** intelligence→performance; proven in production by→deployed with; added per-partner status calibration

**Per-chunk surgical edits (14):**
- L489, L562 — phase prose / LFM2 intro recast: Shopify today, Mercedes targeted H2 2026, AMD laptops today
- L663, L735, L1161 — Nanos uniqueness softened ("No competitor ships an equivalent" → "No rival currently ships a comparable" / "Few competitors ship a comparable")
- L724 — LFM2-24B-A2B tok/s tagged `(Liquid-reported)`; "only direct" → "closest direct"
- L733 — ColBERT "smallest published" tagged `(vendor claim)`; "uniquely suited" → "well-suited"
- L741 — MMAI "1,000+ pharma benchmarks" → "200+ pharma tasks" (correcting overstatement against Insilico's own figure)
- L756 — AMD partner row "first and only AI-PC platform" → "by AMD and Liquid's account, the first... (vendor-supported)"
- L806 — AI21 Jamba "the first non-transformer to scale to frontier quality" → "AI21 positions it as one of the first"
- L859 — Mercedes environment row "(MBUX shipping)" → "(MBUX, production targeted H2 2026)"
- L877 — Meta Muse Spark — added "reportedly"
- L970 — pillar phrase "up to 1,000× smaller than frontier LLMs" tagged `(vendor claim)`
- L1132 (qat glossary) — "Liquid uses" → "Liquid reports using"; structural-advantage framing → measured tradeoff
- L1222 (hf glossary) — "10M cumulative downloads" tagged `(vendor-reported)`

## Hands-off (verified)
All locked facts untouched: layer splits, model size/date pairs, Series A figures, GAIA 86%/90%, Belcak/NVIDIA Research, Gartner 2028/2030 intentional divergence preserved, GSM8K/IFEval Wave-4 fix preserved.

## Verification
- HTML parses 0 errors
- Line count unchanged (1505)
- All 38 `<span class="t">` wrappers preserved
- No "frontier-quality intelligence" or "proven in production" remnants

## Reports
Per-chunk reports in `/home/user/workspace/factcheck/calibration_5/REPORT_C{1..5}.md`.

## Wave 5 — Readability + Generalist Accessibility

Heavy prose-level rewrite executed by 22 parallel Opus 4.8 agents, each owning one isolated chunk of the Study Guide. Rewrote dense, paren-heavy passages so jargon is explained inline as natural prose instead of nested parenthetical asides. Reader floor: a technical generalist (PM, founder, GTM lead) who knows model/benchmark/GPU but does not know GQA, ColBERT, ASIL, MoE, NPU tri-engine, full-duplex, NanoBEIR, ExecuTorch, QAT, or doom-loop/abstention.

### Scope
- 12 narrative chunks (Units 1.1 through 7.3)
- 10 glossary chunks (~90 entries across size, architecture, modality, deployment, retrieval, benchmarks, licensing, compliance, and ecosystem)
- 178 lines modified in place; total line count unchanged
- HTML structure preserved (all spans, anchors, cross-links, data attributes intact)

### What this is not
- **Not a fact-check.** All Wave-4 fact decisions preserved verbatim. Vendor-claim, Liquid-reported, and unverified tags intact.
- **No harmonization.** The SG-internal Gartner 2028 (body) vs 2030 (glossary) split is preserved as-is.

### Key preservations
- Mercedes 3rd/4th-gen MBUX (not collapsed to Gen 4)
- LFM2-8B-A1B (Oct 2025) vs LFM2.5-8B-A1B (May 2026) kept distinct
- LFM2-24B-A2B preserved
- Layer splits (10+6/16; 22+8/30; 18 of 24) intact
- GAIA 86% vs Claude Sonnet 4 90%
- 250M Series A / 2.3B val / 46.6M seed / ~297M total
- GSM8K 82.41 vs Qwen3-4B 68.46 (Liquid-reported)
- Brilliant Halo 299 / LFM2-VL-450M
- Apple IFP ~3B activated (not 20B)
- Belcak / NVIDIA Research / arXiv:2506.02153
- Verbosity penalty direction (LFM2 too verbose, not too short)
- 'Lens(es)' canonical noun preserved
- Unit 7 Naive → Sharp → Ask structure preserved
- 'Read everything twice — charitably, skeptically' spine preserved
- Self-critical asides ('n/p doing rhetorical work,' 'ratified, not validated') preserved with their bite

### Sample before/after (Unit 1.7 — Cartesia voice line)
**Before:** "Cartesia Sonic 3.5 (sub-90ms, vendor-claimed naturalness leadership (the independent Realtime TTS Arena, May 2026, ranks Sonic 3.5 #2 behind Inworld)) leads pure voice benchmarks; Kyutai Moshi owns full-duplex."

**After:** Split into separate sentences so the arena-ranking caveat gets equal billing instead of being buried inside a nested parenthetical, and full-duplex is glossed inline as 'speak and listen at once, like a phone call rather than a walkie-talkie.'

### Methodology
- 22 Opus 4.8 subagents, each owning one isolated line range
- All agents read the same three grounding docs (PLAYBOOK, PROJECT_SCOPE, WORLD_BRIEF) before editing
- Grounding docs themselves audited against the live SG before spawning (see workspace/factcheck/readability_slices/AUDIT_SG_vs_grounding.md)
- No grep, no commits from subagents, no edits outside assigned slice
- Gloss-length precedence rule: short hint for terms wrapped in clickable `<span class="t">` glossary spans; full inline gloss for non-clickable jargon
title: Wave 5: Readability + generalist accessibility rewrite

body:
## Summary

Optimizes `index.html` for mobile browsers and gracefully deprecates desktop-only features (note-taking, reading paths, keyboard shortcuts).

## Mobile rendering (≤640px)
- Topbar fits on 320px wide phones (brand wraps, buttons shrink)
- Nav links, drill chips, and path buttons enlarged to ≥40px tap targets
- Perspective grid collapses to one column; callouts and timeline tighten
- Glossary popover becomes a bottom sheet instead of overflowing
- Lexicon drawer takes full viewport height
- Tables retain horizontal scroll

## Gracefully degraded desktop-only UI
Gated behind `matchMedia('(min-width:641px) and (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)')`:
- Per-section notes textareas — not injected on touch
- Mark-read / progress count — hidden
- Export & reset notes — hidden
- Reading-path picker + floating path bar — hidden
- `j` / `k` / `g` / `/` keyboard shortcuts — not bound
- Lexicon search placeholder drops the `press /` hint

Also covers iPad-in-landscape via `@media (hover:none) and (pointer:coarse)`.

Functional core preserved everywhere: scrolling, TOC, inline glossary terms with tap-to-define popover, full searchable Lexicon, all unit content, deep-dive sections, progress bar.
title: Mobile UX: optimize layout and gracefully degrade desktop-only features
